did.abstract: This collection documents Frank Casier's, and his fellow local residents', campaigns against the Adirondack Park Agency (APA) Act and the actions of the Agency from the 1960s through the 1990s.
did.physloc: The materials are located onsite in the department.

bioghist.head: Biographical History
bioghist.p: Francis David Casier, better known by friends and family as Frank, was born in 1918 in Lyon Mountain, New York. In 1938, Casier attended trade school in Malone before going on to welding school in Hartford, Connecticut a year later. He began his professional career working in shipyards in New York City and New Jersey, but was forced to return to the Adirondacks in 1941 because of a tuberculosis diagnosis. He was treated in a sanatorium in Ray Brook where he stayed until he was cured in 1943. Casier was unable to join the military because of his past bout with tuberculosis and instead enrolled in the Merchant Marines until 1945 when he returned to Ray Book after the tuberculosis resurfaced, now accompanied with malaria. While being treated in Ray Book for the second time, Casier purchased his first property in Saranac Lake, beginning his real estate journey in the Adirondacks. Casier spent the next few years purchasing and selling tax sale properties and founding Casier Utilities Inc, a business he operated for 25 years.

At 32, Casier met his future wife Audrey. The couple married in 1950 and welcomed their only child, David, in 1959. The two were long-time residents of Saranac Lake in the Adirondack Region of New York. Casier's love for Saranac Lake was showcased in the variety of community efforts he and his wife engaged in. He was involved in several civic and environmental activities organized by the community, including the Lion's club and the creation of North Country Community College, where he later served on the Board of Trustees. Above all else, Casier was most heavily involved in local Adirondack property rights organizations. He founded the Adirondack Defense League in 1977, and through this Defense League, he and fellow activists wrote and published The Adirondack Defender. Casier continued to serve his community into the turn of the century and was awarded the Saranac Lake Citizen of the Year in 2007. Casier continued his activist work until he was no longer physically able, passing away at the age of 97 in 2016.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Frank Casier Papers focus largely on opposition to the creation of the Adirondack Park and the Adirondack Park Agency (APA). The collection contains correspondences, APA rules and regulations, letters to the editor, newspaper clippings (a majority of which are from local Adirondack newspapers like the Lake Placid News and Adirondack Daily Enterprise), select issues and drafts of The Adirondack Defender, notes on the Adirondack Park Agency Local Government Review Board, subject files, reports, flyers, political advertising, and video cassettes.

arrangement.head: Arrangement of the Collection
arrangement.p: The collection is arranged into three series: Anti-APA, The Adirondack Defenderr, and Subject Files. All three series are arranged alphabetically.

acqinfo.head: Acquisition Information
acqinfo.p: Frank, Audrey, and David Casier donated the collection to the M.E. Grenander Department of Special Collections & Archives in 2015.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Frank Casier spent decades of his life organizng and petitioning members of the community and legislation to dismantle the Adirondack Park Agency (APA). Materials in this series consist of correspondences, notes from meetings held by the local government review boards on the APA, protest flyers, letters to the editor, APA Rules and Regulations, grievances of Frank Casier and fellow Adirondackers against the The Adirondack Park Agency, notes, and newspaper clippings. This is the largest series in the Frank Casier Papers and is useful for researchers interested in understanding public reactions to any land use regulations and reorganizing done by The Adirondack Park Agency to create the Adirondack Park.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series consists of select Adirondack Defender Issues (Vol. 1, No. 1, Vol. 1 No. 3-5, Vol 2. No. 1-4) published from 1976 to 1978. This series additionally contains drafts, newsletters, correspondences, and notes for upcoming issues of the newspaper. The Adirondack Defender was a small project published by the Adirondack Defense League that Frank Casier and Tony D'Elia started and operated from Casier's home office. What started as letters to the editor to local newspapers grew to an independent Anti-APA political paper. Frank Casier and Tony D'Elia wrote articles for the paper and Melinda Hadley typed up the final product and acted as secretary. Newspapers were circulated for free to members of the mailing list or distributed in local businesses. The goal was to inform Adirondack residents about issues pertaining to the The Adirondack Park Agency and to inspire residents to join the action in petitioning New York government officials to "Abolish the APA". Most often it was used to discuss how public land use reconfiguration by the APA could potentially infringe on the private land of residents. This series would be useful for researchers interested in public reactions to the APA and grassroots organizations.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains correspondences to fellow Adirondackers about local community concerns and organizations, information on the formation of North Country Community College, notes on environmental concerns and legislature, newspaper clippings, publications, and other material that Frank Casier may have been interested in because of his activist work in the Adirondacks but did not pertain to The Adirondack Park Agency.
